section.encryptionKeys.title: Encryption keys
section.encryptionKeys.blurb: At-rest encryption: the active key provider (local keyring, KMS or HSM), how data keys are distributed across key-encryption keys, and key rotation (KEK re-wrap leaves data untouched; DEK rotation re-encrypts the secrets).

mcp.premiumDesc: The AI connector (MCP) requires an active license that grants the “AI connector (MCP)” feature. It stays disabled until a matching license is imported (Security & Compliance → License).
mcp.enableDesc: Opt-in for this organization only. When OFF, no AI client can obtain an access token — every connection attempt is refused at consent. When ON, your users can connect their own AI client and act with their own permissions.
mcp.urlDesc: Share this URL with your users — they paste it into their AI client (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot Studio) as a custom connector, then sign in.
mcp.urlInactive: Inactive until you enable the connector above.
mcp.authDesc: MCP login reuses your existing sign-in (local accounts and any configured SSO / Entra ID). There is nothing extra to configure here — users authenticate the same way they sign in to the app, and the AI is bound to their account.
mcp.authSso: {{count}} SSO provider(s) configured — used for MCP sign-in too.
mcp.authLocal: No SSO provider configured — MCP sign-in uses local accounts. Configure SSO in the Single sign-on section to delegate to Entra ID.
mcp.writesDesc: OFF (default) = the AI can only READ. ON = connected users can also let the AI create / modify projects, tasks, assignments and time entries — always bounded by each user’s own permissions. The consent screen reflects the granted scope.
mcp.writesOn: Write tools are also exposed (create / modify), within each user’s permissions.
mcp.writesOff: Write tools are hidden — the AI observes and suggests only.
mcp.financeDesc: OFF (default) = financial data (rates, budgets, EVM, expenses, portfolio margins) is NEVER returned to AI / API tokens — even for finance-privileged users. ON = users with finance permissions can read it via the AI. Browser app users are unaffected either way.
mcp.clientsDesc: For integrations that do not self-register (e.g. Microsoft Copilot Studio / Power Platform): create a client here, paste its ID + secret into the connector. Claude and ChatGPT don’t need this — they self-register.
mcp.secretOnce: Copy the secret now — it will not be shown again.
mcp.clientCreated: Client created — copy the secret now, it is shown only once.
mcp.connsDesc: Every user’s AI client currently connected to this organization. Disconnect to cut access immediately — the user will have to reconnect. Suspending or deleting a user also cuts their connections automatically.
mcp.confirmDesc: Before a destructive action (delete, notify stakeholders…), the AI must ask the user to confirm, then repeat the call with a one-time token. Applies only to people driving an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT…) — NOT to autonomous agents, which are governed under Agents.
mcp.quotaDesc: Cap how many times a given AI tool may be called per minute, per token — a safety net against a runaway loop that stays invisible to € / token budgets. This adds a frequency dimension to the cost budgets set under Agents. Use “*” as a catch-all for tools without an explicit limit.
mcp.quotaNone: No limit configured — only the per-token rate limit applies.
mcp.quotaInvalid: Enter a valid tool name (vaks_… or *) and a limit ≥ 1.
mcp.usageNone: No AI tool call in the current window.
mcp.usageNote: Live counters (reads included). The audit log keeps the history, but under-counts reads (only writes and audited reads are recorded there).

group.identity.label: Users & Identity
group.identity.blurb: Local accounts, roles and external identity providers.
group.aiAgentManagement.label: AI Agent Management
group.aiAgentManagement.blurb: Govern your AI agents and audit what they cost: policy rules that gate reviews and transitions, and the full usage & cost ledger.
group.org.label: Organization
group.org.blurb: Tenant profile, localization and contracted working time.
group.integrations.label: Integrations
group.integrations.blurb: AI connectors, outbound email, webhooks and API tokens.
group.security.label: Security & Compliance
group.security.blurb: Authentication hardening, password policy, sessions and audit.
group.notifications.label: Notifications & Email
group.notifications.blurb: Branded templates and the org's default notification preferences. Per-user overrides come later — these defaults apply to everyone.
group.automations.label: Automations
group.automations.blurb: Built-in automation rules shipped with the product. Enable each rule and tune its thresholds — alerts go out by email and to any Teams-format webhook subscribed to `automation.alert`. Every automatic action is recorded in the audit log as SYSTEM.
section.automationEngine.title: Automation engine
section.automationEngine.blurb: Global switch and schedule. Daily rules run once a day at the hour below (UTC). Alerts respect the notification quiet hours — avoid placing the daily hour inside them.
section.automationTaskHygiene.title: Task hygiene
section.automationTaskHygiene.blurb: Keeps the boards honest: dormant, overdue, stalled or unassigned tasks are flagged to the right people once a day (one alert per task per week).
setting.automationsEnabled.label: Enable automations
setting.automationsEnabled.desc: Kill switch for the whole engine. When off, no rule runs and nothing is sent.
setting.automationsDailyHour.label: Daily run hour
setting.automationsDailyHour.desc: Hour (0-23, UTC) at which the daily rules are evaluated.
setting.autoOnHoldDormantEnabled.label: Dormant on-hold tasks
setting.autoOnHoldDormantEnabled.desc: Alert the project managers when a task has been on hold without any movement.
setting.autoOnHoldDormantDays.label: Dormant after
setting.autoOnHoldDormantDays.desc: Days on hold without update before the alert.
setting.autoOverdueEnabled.label: Overdue tasks
setting.autoOverdueEnabled.desc: Alert the assignees and the project managers when a task passes its due date without being done.
setting.autoOverdueGraceDays.label: Grace period
setting.autoOverdueGraceDays.desc: Days past the due date before the alert fires.
setting.autoInProgressInactiveEnabled.de: Nudge the assignees when an in-progress task shows no activity.
setting.autoInProgressInactiveDays.label: Stalled after
setting.autoInProgressInactiveDays.desc: Days without activity before the nudge.
setting.autoUnassignedStaleEnabled.label: Unassigned tasks
setting.autoUnassignedStaleEnabled.desc: Alert the project managers when a to-do task still has no assignee.
setting.autoUnassignedStaleDays.label: Unassigned after
setting.autoUnassignedStaleDays.desc: Days since creation before the alert.
Alert the assignees and the project managers when a task stays flagged as blocked by an external provider.
setting.autoExternalBlockedStaleDays.des: Days flagged as blocked by an external provider before the alert.
section.automationDeadlines.title: Deadlines
section.automationDeadlines.blurb: Milestones that will not land on time. The due-date reminder itself lives under Notifications & Email.
section.automationWorkload.title: Workload
section.automationWorkload.blurb: Capacity signals based on real availability (work schedule, time off and holidays deducted). Alerts go to the team leads of the person concerned.
section.automationTimesheet.title: Timesheet
section.automationTimesheet.blurb: Weekly checks run on the finished week, on the day and hour set below.
section.automationBudget.title: Budget alerts
section.automationBudget.blurb: Budget signals on active projects that have a budget set. Alerts go to the project managers.
section.automationProjects.title: Projects
section.automationProjects.blurb: Whole-project signals, alerted to the project managers.
setting.autoMilestoneAtRiskEnabled.label: Milestones at risk
setting.autoMilestoneAtRiskEnabled.desc: Alert the project managers when a milestone is approaching while some of its predecessors are still unfinished.
setting.autoMilestoneAtRiskDays.label: Look ahead
setting.autoMilestoneAtRiskDays.desc: Days before the milestone date to start checking.
setting.autoOverloadEnabled.label: Overloaded people
setting.autoOverloadEnabled.desc: Alert the team leads when someone's allocations exceed their capacity next week.
setting.autoOverloadThreshold.label: Overload threshold
setting.autoOverloadThreshold.desc: Percentage of available capacity above which the alert fires.
setting.autoUnderloadEnabled.label: Spare capacity
setting.autoUnderloadEnabled.desc: Alert the team leads when someone is under-allocated — useful for staffing upcoming work.
setting.autoUnderloadThreshold.label: Underload threshold
setting.autoUnderloadThreshold.desc: Percentage of available capacity below which the alert fires.
setting.autoUnderloadWeeks.label: Look-ahead window
setting.autoUnderloadWeeks.desc: Number of weeks considered when measuring under-allocation.
setting.autoUtilizationEnabled.label: Billable utilization
setting.autoUtilizationEnabled.desc: Alert the team leads when someone logs too little of their time on billable projects. Measured per person on the finished week — billability is a project property, so a per-project ratio would always be 100% or 0%.
setting.autoUtilizationThreshold.label: Utilization target
setting.autoUtilizationThreshold.desc: Share of logged time expected on billable projects.
setting.autoTimesheetReminderEnabled.des: Remind people whose timesheet covers less than the target share of their capacity.
setting.autoTimesheetReminderThreshold.d: Share of the expected capacity below which the reminder is sent.
setting.autoTimesheetReminderWeekday.des: Day the weekly rules run — 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday.
setting.autoTimesheetReminderHour.label: Weekly run hour
setting.autoTimesheetReminderHour.desc: Hour (0-23, UTC) the weekly rules run.
setting.autoOvertimeEnabled.label: High overtime
setting.autoOvertimeEnabled.desc: Alert the team leads when someone declares a lot of overtime in a week.
setting.autoOvertimeHours.label: Overtime threshold
setting.autoOvertimeHours.desc: Declared overtime hours in a single week above which the alert fires.
setting.autoBudgetThresholdEnabled.label: Budget thresholds
setting.autoBudgetThresholdEnabled.desc: Alert when the actual cost of a project crosses a share of its budget.
setting.autoBudgetThresholdTiers.label: Thresholds
setting.autoBudgetThresholdTiers.desc: Comma-separated percentages, e.g. "80,100". One alert per threshold crossed. Five maximum.
setting.autoForecastOverrunEnabled.label: Forecast overrun
setting.autoForecastOverrunEnabled.desc: Alert when the projected cost at completion exceeds the budget, even though the actual spend is still within it.
setting.autoProjectEndSoonEnabled.label: Projects ending with open work
setting.autoProjectEndSoonEnabled.desc: Alert when an active project reaches its end date while tasks are still open.
setting.autoProjectEndSoonDays.label: Look ahead
setting.autoProjectEndSoonDays.desc: Days before the project end date to start checking.
setting.autoProjectInactiveEnabled.label: Idle active projects
setting.autoProjectInactiveEnabled.desc: Alert when an active project shows no activity at all — no task update, no logged time, no comment.
setting.autoProjectInactiveDays.label: Idle after
setting.autoProjectInactiveDays.desc: Days without any activity before the alert.
section.automationSkills.title: Skills
section.automationSkills.blurb: Checked when a task is created, not on a schedule.
section.automationAgents.title: AI agents
section.automationAgents.blurb: Cost and review signals for AI agents. Note: tasks an agent keeps failing are already handled by the poison-task escalation under Agent policies — it removes the agent rather than just warning.
setting.autoAutoplanOverflowEnabled.desc: Alert the project managers when an applied auto-plan cannot fit some tasks before their due date. Only fires on apply, never on preview.
setting.autoTimeOffConflictEnabled.label: Time off vs plan
setting.autoTimeOffConflictEnabled.desc: Alert the project managers when approved time off overlaps allocations already planned — the plan goes stale the moment the leave is entered.
setting.autoAllocationWindowMissedEnable: Alert the allocated people and the project managers when a task had time allocated for it, but its planned window closed and it never left To do. Based on status, not on logged time — an empty timesheet is the normal case without daily entries.
setting.autoAllocationWindowMissedGraceD: Days after the window closes before the alert fires.
setting.autoSkillGapEnabled.label: Missing skill on new tasks
setting.autoSkillGapEnabled.desc: Alert the project managers when a task requires a skill that nobody on the project covers (direct members and members of assigned teams, expired skills excluded).
setting.autoAgentBudgetEnabled.label: Agent budget running out
setting.autoAgentBudgetEnabled.desc: Warn before agents get blocked. The daily, monthly, per-project and per-task caps are enforced at claim time; this alerts at the threshold below so the cap can be raised in time.
setting.autoAgentBudgetThreshold.label: Budget warning threshold
setting.autoAgentBudgetThreshold.desc: Share of an agent budget above which the warning fires.
setting.autoDeliverableStaleEnabled.desc: Nudge the project managers when a submitted deliverable has been waiting for review — the work stays blocked until someone reviews it.
setting.autoDeliverableStaleHours.label: Waiting for
setting.autoDeliverableStaleHours.desc: Hours a deliverable may sit in review before the nudge.
group.skills.label: Skills
group.skills.blurb: Skills referenced in the organization. Skills help steer task assignment and auto-planning toward the right profiles.
group.customization.label: Customization
group.customization.blurb: Tailor Vaks to your process: define custom fields on tasks and projects.
section.customFieldsSection.title: Custom fields
section.customFieldsSection.blurb: Add your own fields to tasks and projects (reference, environment, sign-off…). A field can be restricted to specific projects.
section.customFieldsGovernance.title: Custom fields governance
section.customFieldsGovernance.blurb: Who may create and edit custom field definitions.
setting.customFieldsWriteMode.label: Who can manage custom fields
setting.customFieldsWriteMode.desc: A custom field shapes your data model, so the default is admin-only. Each level includes the previous ones.
section.customStatusesSection.title: Custom Status
section.customStatusesSection.blurb: Add sub-statuses under the built-in statuses (e.g. “Client validation” under In review, “Waiting on client” under On hold). Shown on the board inside the parent column. A sub-status can be restricted to specific projects.
section.customStatusesGovernance.title: Custom Status governance
section.customStatusesGovernance.blurb: Who may create and edit sub-statuses.
setting.customStatusesWriteMode.label: Who can manage sub-statuses
setting.customStatusesWriteMode.desc: Sub-statuses shape every project board, so the default is admin-only. Each level includes the previous ones.
group.data.label: Data Management
group.data.blurb: Soft-delete cleanup and GDPR data portability.
section.accounts.title: Accounts
section.users.title: Users
section.users.blurb: Everyone with an account — search, roles and status.
section.teams.title: Teams
section.teams.blurb: Working groups, their leads and members.
section.roles.title: Roles
section.roles.blurb: System roles available in this organization and the permissions they grant.
section.sso.title: Single sign-on
section.sso.blurb: Federate sign-in with your identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID via OIDC). JIT provisioning, account linking and role mapping.
section.profile.title: Profile
section.license.title: License
section.license.blurb: Your license: covered enterprise features, expiry, and import of a new license file. Core features always stay free.
section.docTemplates.title: Document templates
section.docTemplates.blurb: Word templates used when exporting documents (project charter, etc.).
section.projectMgmt.title: Project management
section.projectMgmt.blurb: Who is allowed to create billable and non-billable projects.
section.workingTime.title: Working time
section.finance.title: Finance
section.billingExportSchedule.title: Scheduled billing export
section.billingExportSchedule.blurb: Automatically email a billing export (CSV or XLSX) to a list of recipients on a weekly or monthly schedule. The export covers the previous full period (last week or last month).
section.aiConnectors.title: AI connectors (MCP)
section.smtp.title: Email (SMTP)
section.smtp.blurb: Relay used for outbound notifications. The password can be entered here (encrypted at rest) or mounted at deploy time via the SMTP_PASSWORD secret.
section.api.title: API
section.webhooksGovernance.title: Webhooks — governance
section.webhooks.title: Webhooks
section.webhooks.blurb: Outbound HTTP callbacks fired on task / comment / project events. Each delivery is signed (HMAC-SHA256) so the receiver can verify authenticity.
section.orgApiKeys.title: Organization API keys
section.orgApiKeys.blurb: Organization-level API keys (service identity, read-only). For integrations that consume the public API without acting on behalf of a user. The secret is shown only once.
section.authentication.title: Authentication
section.passwordPolicy.title: Password policy
section.auditLog.title: Audit log
section.auditLog.blurb: Append-only trace of who did what, when: sign-ins (successful and failed), MFA, API tokens, role changes, settings, webhooks and every mutation. JSON Lines / CEF export. No deletion possible — only retention purge erases.
section.siem.title: SIEM / syslog forwarding
section.siem.blurb: Real-time forwarding of the audit log to an external collector, real-time security alerts, and log retention.
section.securityAlerts.title: Security alerts
section.securityAlerts.blurb: Real-time detection on the audit log. When the threshold is crossed: email to all admins + webhook `audit.alert` (Teams, automation, SIEM push). At most one alert per account per hour.
section.logRetention.title: Log retention
section.masterSwitch.title: Master switch
section.masterSwitch.blurb: Stops every outbound notification in one click. Useful during incidents or SMTP migrations — no need to toggle each event below.
section.senderIdentity.title: Sender identity
section.defaultPreferences.title: Default preferences
section.deliveryCadence.title: Delivery cadence
section.deliveryCadence.blurb: Bundle non-urgent notifications and prevent night-time pings.
section.skillsSettings.title: Settings
section.skillsLifecycleClose.title: Lifecycle — skill growth on close
section.skillsLifecycleDecay.title: Lifecycle — decrement by inactivity (decay)
section.skillsCatalog.title: Catalogue
section.skillsCatalog.blurb: Repository of available skills. Renaming or deleting a skill impacts every task and user that references it.
section.skillsImport.title: Bulk import (CSV)
section.skillsImport.blurb: Bulk import of user levels via CSV `email,skill,level[,category]` (4th category column optional). Optionally creates missing skills. Idempotent.
section.skillsLevelScale.title: Level scale
section.skillsLevelScale.blurb: Gives a semantic label to each level (e.g. 1=Discovery, 3=Autonomous, 5=Senior, 7=Expert). Org-wide — applied to every view that shows a level (user skills, required level on tasks).
section.retentionCleanup.title: Retention & cleanup
section.portability.title: Portability
setting.defaultRole.label: Default role for new users
setting.defaultRole.desc: Role assigned when a member is created or invited.
setting.bulkImport.label: Bulk import users
setting.bulkImport.desc: Provision many accounts at once from a CSV file.
setting.orgName.label: Organization name
setting.orgName.desc: Shown in the sidebar, emails and exports.
setting.orgLogoUrl.label: Organization logo
setting.orgLogoUrl.desc: PNG, JPEG, SVG, WebP or GIF — max 1 MB. Used in the sidebar, exports, and as the default logo for outbound email notifications. Upload replaces the previous logo immediately.
setting.locale.label: Default locale (formatting)
setting.locale.desc: Date & number formatting for new users (BCP47 region). Separate from the UI language below.
setting.defaultLanguage.label: Default UI language
setting.defaultLanguage.desc: Interface language for users who have not picked their own. Each user can override it from the language selector in the top bar.
setting.hoursPerDay.label: Hours per working day
setting.hoursPerDay.desc: Capacity baseline per person, per day. Applies to every user that has no custom schedule.
setting.defaultWorkDays.label: Default working days
setting.defaultWorkDays.desc: Days of the week users work on by default. Days that are off carry zero capacity in the workload and timeline grids.
setting.weekStart.label: Week starts on
setting.weekStart.desc: First column of the workload & timeline grids.
setting.autoplanConcentration.label: Auto-plan concentration
setting.autoplanConcentration.desc: Default for the "how many people per task" trade-off when auto-plan assigns tasks. Focus favors fewer people; spread restores the historical one-person-per-task behavior. Overridable per run in Workload.
setting.holidayCountry.label: Default holiday country
setting.holidayCountry.desc: Default country used for the list of holidays shown in Workload and Timeline. Each user can override this country on their profile to apply the holidays of their own country.
setting.fiscalYearStart.label: Fiscal year start month
setting.fiscalYearStart.desc: Month when the fiscal year starts. Used by global finance for quarter / half-year / fiscal-year filters.
setting.aiEnabled.label: Enable AI suggestions
setting.aiEnabled.desc: Surface suggested tasks & assignees in the product.
setting.suggestTasks.label: suggest_tasks endpoint
setting.suggestTasks.desc: MCP tool that proposes follow-up tasks.
setting.suggestAssignees.label: suggest_assignees endpoint
setting.suggestAssignees.desc: MCP tool that recommends the best assignee.
setting.smtpHost.label: SMTP host
setting.smtpPort.label: SMTP port
setting.smtpPort.desc: Usually 587 for STARTTLS, 465 for SSL/TLS, 25 for none.
setting.smtpEncryption.label: Encryption
setting.smtpAuthMode.label: Authentication
setting.smtpAuthMode.desc: Anonymous = no login (internal relay). Password = SASL with SMTP_PASSWORD from the docker secret.
setting.smtpUser.label: SMTP username
setting.smtpUser.desc: Only used when authentication = password. Set the matching password below, or leave it to the SMTP_PASSWORD deploy secret.
setting.billingExportEnabled.label: Enable scheduled export
setting.billingExportFrequency.label: Frequency
setting.billingExportWeekDay.label: Day of week (weekly)
setting.billingExportMonthDay.label: Day of month (monthly)
setting.billingExportHour.label: Send hour (UTC)
setting.billingExportFormat.label: File format
setting.billingExportRecipients.label: Recipients
setting.billingExportSendNow.label: Send now
setting.billingExportSendNow.desc: Immediately send the billing export for the previous period to all configured recipients.
setting.smtpTest.label: Connection test
setting.smtpTest.desc: Send a real "test" email to your address using the current settings.
setting.apiVersion.label: Public API version
setting.apiVersion.desc: Versioned REST API consumed by the web app and integrations.
setting.apiTokens.label: Org-level API tokens
setting.webhooksManagePolicy.label: Who can create a webhook
setting.webhooksManagePolicy.desc: Beyond the Org Admin (who always can). 'project_manager' = a PM connects THEIR project / a lead THEIR team in self-service; 'portfolio_manager' = reserved for portfolio PMs; 'admin' = admin only.
setting.webhooksDomainAllowlist.label: Allowed domains (allowlist)
setting.webhooksDomainAllowlist.desc: List of allowed target domains, separated by commas or spaces (e.g. webhook.office.com, hooks.slack.com). Empty = any public host allowed. Anti-SSRF protection (loopback / private IPs) applies in all cases.
setting.webhooksEntraTenantAllowlist.des: GUID of the allowed Microsoft tenant(s) as destination. Find it in Azure Portal → Microsoft Entra ID → Overview → "Tenant ID". When set, a webhook to Teams (*.webhook.office.com, tenant in …@<tenantId>/…) or Power Automate Default environment (*.environment.api.powerplatform.com, tenant encoded in the host) is only accepted if its tenant is in the list — anti-leak toward a foreign tenant. Custom Power Platform environments cannot be verified (refused when the allowlist is active). Empty = no Entra restriction.
setting.requireMfa.label: Require MFA for local accounts
setting.requireMfa.desc: Every local-password member must enrol an authenticator (TOTP). Break-glass accounts always have MFA on.
setting.ssoOnly.label: Require SSO (disable local password sign-in)
setting.ssoOnly.desc: Members must sign in through an identity provider. Local password sign-in is refused for everyone EXCEPT break-glass accounts (per-user toggle in the user list). ⚠ Make sure at least one admin has break-glass enabled WITH a password set before turning this on, or you may lock yourself out.
setting.sessionTimeout.label: Session idle timeout
setting.sessionTimeout.desc: Sign a member out after this much inactivity. Set to 0 to disable (members are never signed out for being idle).
setting.lockoutMaxAttempts.label: Lockout threshold
setting.lockoutMaxAttempts.desc: Lock the account after this many consecutive failed sign-ins.
setting.lockoutDuration.label: Lockout duration
setting.lockoutDuration.desc: How long the account stays locked after the threshold is reached.
setting.activeSessions.label: Active sessions
setting.activeSessions.desc: Currently signed-in sessions across the org.
setting.forceLogout.label: Force logout everyone
setting.pwMinLength.label: Minimum length
setting.pwComplexity.label: Complexity
setting.pwExpiry.label: Password expiry
setting.pwExpiry.desc: Force a change after this many days · 0 = never.
setting.pwHistory.label: Prevent reuse
setting.pwHistory.desc: Block the last N passwords from being reused.
setting.checkCommonPasswords.label: Block common passwords
setting.checkCommonPasswords.desc: Reject passwords from a built-in list of the most leaked passwords (offline, ~500 entries). Recommended on.
setting.syslogEnabled.label: Forward to a SIEM
setting.syslogEnabled.desc: Kill switch. When disabled, the log stays viewable in the app but nothing is sent.
setting.syslogHost.label: Collector host
setting.syslogHost.desc: DNS name or IP of the syslog receiver.
setting.syslogPort.label: Port
setting.syslogProtocol.label: Transport
setting.syslogProtocol.desc: TLS recommended — the log contains sensitive data (IPs, emails).
setting.syslogCaPem.label: Collector CA (PEM)
setting.syslogCaPem.desc: CA certificate to trust if the collector presents an internal / self-signed certificate. Empty = system store.
setting.syslogClientCertPem.label: mTLS client certificate (PEM)
setting.syslogClientCertPem.desc: For collectors that require mutual authentication. The (public) certificate lives here; the PRIVATE KEY is mounted on the worker via the Swarm secret `syslog_client_key` — never in the database. One key per deployment. Empty = no mTLS.
setting.syslogMinSeverity.label: Minimum severity
setting.syslogMinSeverity.desc: INFO = everything (including every mutation); CRITICAL = only security events.
setting.syslogTest.label: Connection test
setting.syslogTest.desc: Sends an audit.test message to the collector with the SAVED configuration (save first). The result appears here after a few seconds.
setting.alertsLoginFailuresEnabled.label: Brute-force alert
setting.alertsLoginFailuresEnabled.desc: Alert when a single account accumulates sign-in failures. Recommended on.
setting.alertsLoginFailuresThreshold.des: Number of sign-in failures on a single account that triggers the alert.
setting.alertsLoginFailuresWindow.label: Detection window
setting.alertsLoginFailuresWindow.desc: Failures are counted over this sliding window.
setting.retentionDays.label: Audit entry retention
setting.retentionDays.desc: Older entries are purged by a daily cron. The only deletion mechanism for the log.
setting.archiveEnabled.label: Archive before purge
setting.archiveEnabled.desc: Exports entries as gzip JSONL to object storage (Garage) BEFORE deletion — unlimited cold retention for compliance. Fail-safe: if archiving fails, the purge is skipped.
setting.notifEnabled.label: Enable email notifications
setting.notifEnabled.desc: Kill switch. When off, no email is sent regardless of the preferences below.
setting.notifLogoUrl.label: Email header logo
setting.notifLogoUrl.desc: Override URL of the logo shown at the top of every notification email. Leave empty to inherit the organization logo (Organization → Profile). Falls back to the From name as text if both are empty.
setting.notifAccentColor.label: Template accent colour
setting.notifAccentColor.desc: Buttons and links in outbound email.
setting.notifFromName.label: From name
setting.notifFromAddress.label: From address
setting.notifFromAddress.desc: The email shown to recipients. Must be on a domain accepted by your SMTP relay.
setting.notifReplyTo.label: Reply-to address
setting.notifReplyTo.desc: Where replies go (e.g. a real inbox or support address). Leave empty to let replies bounce off the From address.
setting.notifPreview.label: Preview template
setting.notifPreview.desc: Render an assignment email with the branding above (opens in a new tab).
setting.notifOnAssignment.label: On assignment
setting.notifOnAssignment.desc: Email a member when a task is assigned to them.
setting.notifOnMention.label: On @mention
setting.notifOnMention.desc: Email a member when they're mentioned in a comment.
setting.notifOnDueDate.label: On approaching due date
setting.notifOnDueDate.desc: Remind assignees before a task is due.
setting.notifDueLeadDays.label: Due-date lead time
setting.notifDueLeadDays.desc: Days before the due date when the reminder is sent.
setting.notifOnStatusChange.label: On status change
setting.notifOnStatusChange.desc: Notify watchers when a task moves columns.
setting.notifOnOverEstimate.label: On estimate overrun
setting.notifOnOverEstimate.desc: Email the project managers when the cumulative logged time on a task crosses its estimate (one mail per crossing).
setting.notifDigest.label: Email digest
setting.notifDigest.desc: Bundled summary instead of per-event mail.
setting.notifDigestHour.label: Digest delivery hour
setting.notifDigestHour.desc: Hour (0-23, UTC for now) at which the daily/weekly digest is dispatched.
setting.notifQuietHoursStart.label: Quiet hours start
setting.notifQuietHoursStart.desc: Hour (0-23, UTC) — no email is sent from this time. Leave empty to disable quiet hours.
setting.notifQuietHoursEnd.label: Quiet hours end
setting.notifQuietHoursEnd.desc: Hour (0-23, UTC) — emails resume from this time.
setting.skillsMaxLevel.label: Maximum level
setting.skillsMaxLevel.desc: Upper bound of the level a user can reach on a skill (1..N). Used everywhere: user level editor, desired level per task, scoring of suggestions and auto-planning.
setting.skillsSelfEditEnabled.label: Self-editing by users
setting.skillsSelfEditEnabled.desc: If enabled, each user can edit their own skill levels. Otherwise, only Org Admins and the Team Leads of the user's teams can do so.
setting.skillsCatalogWriteMode.label: Who can create a skill
setting.skillsCatalogWriteMode.desc: Determines who can add, rename or delete a skill from the catalogue. Each level includes all the previous ones.
setting.skillsAutoBumpOnProjectClose.des: If enabled, each time a project moves to COMPLETED, the participants' UserSkill are incremented on the project's ProjectSkill (created if missing). The skills history builds up naturally over projects — this is the business function that makes Skills useful in a services company.
setting.skillsAutoBumpDelta.label: Levels added per closed project
setting.skillsAutoBumpDelta.desc: Capped by the maximum level. Keep at 1 unless special case (one project = +1 level).
setting.skillsDecayEnabled.label: Automatic decrement of unused skills
setting.skillsDecayEnabled.desc: If enabled, a daily cron decrements UserSkill untouched for the chosen period. Models forgetting / loss of practice. When the level reaches 0, the skill is removed from the user. Opt-in option (disabled by default).
setting.skillsDecayPeriodDays.label: Inactivity period before decrement
setting.skillsDecayPeriodDays.desc: Number of days without an update to a UserSkill before it is decremented. Default 365 (one year).
setting.skillsDecayDelta.label: Levels removed per period
setting.skillsDecayDelta.desc: How many levels are removed at each decay cycle. Keep at 1 (the skill descends slowly, no jumping a level).
setting.autoPurge.label: Auto-purge soft-deleted records
setting.autoPurge.desc: When ON, a background job permanently erases trashed items older than the grace period below. OFF by default — nothing is auto-deleted until you enable it.
setting.purgeAfter.label: Purge after
setting.purgeAfter.desc: Grace period (in years) before auto-purge erases soft-deleted data. Only applies to automatic purge — the manual "Purge now" button ignores it.
setting.purgeNow.label: Purge now
setting.exportData.label: Export organization data
setting.exportData.desc: Full machine-readable export for GDPR / portability.

setting.teamsProvTenantId.label: Entra tenant ID

setting.teamsProvClientId.label: Client ID (app registration)
setting.teamsProvClientId.desc: GUID of the dedicated Entra app, with Graph application permissions (Team.Create, TeamMember.ReadWrite.All, Channel.Create) + admin consent.
setting.teamsProvClientSecret.label: Client secret

setting.teamsProvCertThumbprint.label: Certificate thumbprint (x5t)
setting.teamsProvCertThumbprint.desc: Secretless certificate auth (private_key_jwt). Copy the thumbprint from Entra > Certificates after uploading the public .cer. Set it together with the private key — it then takes precedence over the client secret.
setting.teamsProvPrivateKey.label: Private key (PEM PKCS#8)

setting.teamsProvNamePattern.label: Team name pattern

setting.teamsProvChannelLayout.label: Channel layout
setting.teamsProvChannelLayout.desc: Layout of the created channels (including General). Posts = classic post-and-reply; Threads = chat-style threading. Teams uses Posts by default.
setting.teamsProvVisibility.label: Team visibility
setting.teamsProvVisibility.desc: Private = invitation only; Public = visible across the organization. Cannot be changed after creation.
setting.teamsProvMembership.label: Who to invite
setting.teamsProvMembership.desc: assigned_teams = members of the teams assigned to the project; project_members = explicit project access; both = de-duplicated union. Only accounts linked to Entra (SSO/SCIM) can be invited; local accounts are ignored.
setting.teamsProvRemoveOnLeave.label: Remove on leaving the project
setting.teamsProvRemoveOnLeave.desc: Opt-in. If enabled, a member removed from the project is removed from the Teams team. Disabled by default (no surprise removals).
setting.teamsProvArchiveOnClose.label: Archive on close
setting.teamsProvArchiveOnClose.desc: Archives the team (read-only, reversible) when the project leaves ACTIVE. Re-activation un-archives it.
setting.teamsProvTest.label: Test the Graph connection
setting.teamsProvTest.desc: Verifies that a client-credentials token can be obtained and that team creation is permitted.

section.diagnostics.blurb: Generates a diagnostic snapshot (DB/Redis/storage health, job queues, redacted settings, recent errors) to send us in case of an incident. The procedure also indicates which infrastructure logs (Docker, reverse proxy, HA database) to collect on the hosts.
users.seatLicensedDesc: Consumes a license seat and can access the full app.
users.seatNoneDesc: No seat consumed and no dashboard access. An admin keeps the admin portal only; a non-admin cannot access the app.
users.agentAdminDesc: Can manage all AI agents org-wide (identities, tokens, directories, policies) without full admin rights. Stacks on the org role above.
users.noSeatPillHint: This account has no license seat and cannot access the app.
users.adminOnlyPillHint: Admin portal only — no license seat, no dashboard access.
users.seatsUsedHint: Licensed users (consuming a seat) vs the license cap.

teams.autoLicenseHint: Every active member of this team gets a license seat (within the license cap). Ideal for the SCIM/Entra group of licensed users: being added grants a seat, being removed frees it.
section.agents.title: AI agents
section.agents.blurb: AI agent identities: owner, trust level, capabilities, tokens and directory sync. Separate from human members — agents never consume a seat.
agents.intro: AI agents are first-class accounts with a mandatory human owner. They authenticate with a dedicated API token (never a password), act within their capabilities only, and every action is audited with its justification. Suspending the owner instantly disables the agent.
agents.empty: No agent yet. Create one manually, or connect an agent directory below.
agents.quotaCta: Unlock unlimited agents + keyless federation — free trial →
agents.quotaReachedHint: Free agent limit reached — upgrade to add more.

agents.mintScopesHint: A token carries exactly the rights of the capabilities ticked above, frozen at issue time. Change the capabilities and the existing tokens do NOT follow: tick first, save, then issue a new token.
agents.confirmRevokeToken: Revoke this token for “{{name}}”? The agent loses access immediately.
agents.suspended: Agent suspended — its tokens no longer work.
agents.confirmDelete: Delete agent “{{name}}”? Its tokens are revoked; history (comments, audit) is kept.
agents.ownerHelp: Accountable human. If the owner is suspended or removed, the agent stops working.
agents.trustHelp: Drives future policies and deliverable verification requirements. New agents start as Draft only.
agents.capabilitiesHelp: Effective rights = role ∩ token ∩ capabilities. Finance, clients, administration and timesheet are structurally out of reach.
agents.created: Agent created. Issue a token so it can authenticate.
agents.tokenModalBlurb: Copy this token now — it is shown only once. It expires automatically (90 days by default) and can be revoked here at any time.
agents.connectorsBlurb: Import agent identities from your platform (Microsoft Entra Agent ID first). Synced agents arrive suspended-by-capability (read-only, Draft only) and without token — a human activates them.
agents.confirmDeleteConnector: Delete connector “{{name}}”? Already imported agents are kept.
agents.secretKeepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current secret
agents.defaultOwnerHelp: Used when the platform does not expose a native owner. Agents without a resolvable owner are skipped.
agents.searchPlaceholder: Search agents by name, owner or model…
agents.noTokens: No active token. Issue one so the agent can authenticate.
agents.saveFirstForTokens: Save the agent first, then issue an API token for it.
section.agentDirectories.title: Agent directories
section.agentDirectories.blurb: Import AI agent identities from an external platform (Microsoft Entra Agent ID). Synced agents arrive read-only and without a token — a human activates them. Encrypted at rest.
section.ciVerification.title: CI verification
section.ciVerification.blurb: Receive signed CI results (GitHub Actions or a generic HMAC signer) as proof for agent deliverables. vaks-pm never connects out — CI pushes a signed result, we verify the HMAC. Shared secret encrypted at rest.
ci.blurb: Connect a CI signer so agent deliverables can be backed by signed proof (method ci_signed). vaks-pm never reaches out: CI pushes a signed result to the webhook URL below, and we verify the HMAC signature against the shared secret. Enable the ci_signed capability on a project to require it.
ci.empty: No CI signer yet. Add GitHub Actions or a generic HMAC signer to accept signed CI results.
ci.secretHelp: The same secret you set on the CI webhook. Used to verify the HMAC signature of every incoming result. Encrypted at rest, never shown again.
ci.confirmDelete: Remove the CI signer “{{name}}”? Incoming results from it will no longer be accepted.
docsources.blurb: Independent external file sources that AI agents can read as working context (live proxy — nothing is copied). SharePoint document reading is configured under Collaboration spaces (it reuses the Teams identity). Per-project and per-org kill-switches apply, and every read is audited.
docsources.emptyIndependent: No independent document source yet. SharePoint document reading is set up under Collaboration spaces (Microsoft Teams card). Standalone connectors (Google Drive, S3, WebDAV) will appear here.
docsources.sp.testHelp: Test the full chain (site resolution, grant, listing) against a provisioned project without going through an agent.
docsources.sp.projectIdPlaceholder: Project ID (UUID) of a provisioned project
agents.connectorsEmpty: No directory connector yet. Add one to import agents from your platform.
section.agentPolicies.title: Policies
section.agentPolicies.blurb: Governance rules for AI agents: require review, deny or notify based on labels, trust level, estimate or transition — plus review backpressure.
agentPolicies.backpressureDesc: Agents are throttled by the human review throughput. When a project already has this many tasks waiting in review, an agent is refused from pushing more into the queue and retries later. 0 = unlimited.
agentPolicies.requireRunDesc: When enabled, an agent must declare its consumption (tokens / cost via report_run) on a task before it can submit it for review. Guarantees the budget spent per task is always tracked. Only affects agents.
agentPolicies.requireRunToggle: Block review submission until a run is declared
agentPolicies.preauthDesc: When enabled, an agent is refused a task at claim time if the task's estimated cost (its own historical average cost per task) would push spend over a budget envelope — instead of only blocking after the budget is already exceeded. Fails open until the agent has history (first tasks are never blocked). Only affects agents.
agentPolicies.preauthToggle: Refuse claim when the estimated task cost would exceed the remaining budget
agentPolicies.leaseDesc: An agent that claims a task holds it only for this long, and extends the lease with a heartbeat while it works. If it dies (crash, lost connectivity) the lease lapses and the task is returned to the pool (back to TODO, retry count incremented) instead of staying blocked. Humans are never affected. 0 disables the mechanism.
agentPolicies.breakerDesc: Budget envelopes are checked at claim time, but a runaway agent burns them mid-task. Whenever an agent declares a run that consumes an envelope, its owner is alerted and the agent is told to stop. Enable this to also take the task away from it right there (claim and assignment removed, task waits for a human) — the work already produced stays attached to the task.
agentPolicies.breakerToggle: Take the task away from the agent when an envelope is exhausted
section.agentRuns.title: Usage & Cost Ledger
section.agentRuns.blurb: Every run declared by an AI agent: cost, tokens, model, project and task. The audit log of AI consumption.
agentRuns.desc: Every run declared by an AI agent, newest first. The declared cost is what is billed; the reference cost is recomputed server-side from the tokens and the agent profile rates — a large gap is what the anomaly filter catches.
agentPolicies.briefPlaceholder.role: e.g. you write internal technical documentation from existing sources (tickets, meeting notes, code). You never do external research.
agentPolicies.briefPlaceholder.outputCon: e.g. English, markdown, sentence-case headings. Always cite your sources at the end. No table wider than 5 columns.
agentPolicies.briefPlaceholder.deliveryT: e.g. put the document in the task deliverable (content field). Do not create a SharePoint page, do not send email.
agentPolicies.briefPlaceholder.outOfScop: e.g. never touch production configuration. Never invent a figure: if data is missing, ask in a comment and wait for the answer.
agentPolicies.rulesDesc: Each rule matches a task context and applies an action. All predicates set must match (AND); an empty predicate is ignored. Evaluated at claim time and at auto-close. In observe mode a match is only logged.
agentPolicies.empty: No rules — agents follow the default governance only. Add a rule to constrain them.
agents.skillsHint: What this agent can do. The level encodes its reliability on that kind of task, and gates which tasks it can pull (next_task).
agents.inboundHeading: Inbound — a platform declares its agents
agents.inbound.registration.title: Agent registration API
agents.inbound.registration.blurb: Let an external platform (self-hosted agents, LangGraph, n8n…) declare its AI agents in Vaks. Registered agents arrive read-only, without a token — a human activates them and mints their token. Uses an organization key scoped to agent management only.
agents.inbound.registration.epRegister: Idempotent upsert of an agent by externalId (arrives DRAFT_ONLY, no token).
section.collabSpaces.title: Collaboration spaces
section.collabSpaces.blurb: Automatically create a collaboration space when a project becomes ACTIVE, and invite its members. Microsoft Teams is available today; the space can also be created by an external tool that declares it back to Vaks.
collab.intro: One card per provider. The space is created when the project becomes ACTIVE, and archived when it leaves that state (configurable). Credentials are encrypted at rest and never shown again.
collab.confirmDeleteTeams: Remove the Microsoft Teams connector? Its configuration (tenant, app, secret) will be cleared and provisioning disabled. Existing Teams already provisioned are not affected.
collab.confirmDeleteSharepoint: Remove the SharePoint document connector? The identity model and reader app will be cleared and document reading disabled.
collab.enableField: Enabled (create a space on project activation)
collab.msteams.blurb: Creates a Microsoft Teams team with its channels and invites the members. Requires a dedicated Entra app registration with Graph application permissions (Team.Create, TeamMember.ReadWrite.All, Channel.Create) and admin consent. Only accounts linked to Entra (SSO/SCIM) can be invited.
collab.confirmDeleteSlack: Remove the Slack connector? The bot token and channel settings will be cleared and provisioning disabled. Channels already created are not affected.
collab.slack.blurb: Creates a Slack channel and invites the members, matched by email to a Slack account. Requires a Slack app with a bot token (xoxb-…) granted the scopes to create channels, invite users, and look up users by email — no Entra dependency, works standalone.
collab.slack.field.botToken.label: Bot token
collab.slack.field.botToken.help: The xoxb-… bot token of a Slack app installed on your workspace, with channels:manage (public channels) or groups:write (private channels) plus users:read.email. Encrypted at rest, never shown again — leave empty to keep the current token.
collab.slack.field.channelPrefix.label: Channel name prefix
collab.slack.field.channelPrefix.help: Prepended to the slugified project name, e.g. proj- → #proj-website-revamp.
collab.slack.field.visibility.label: Channel visibility
collab.slack.field.visibility.help: Private or public channel. Not changeable after creation — a Slack limitation.
collab.slack.field.invite.label: Invite members
collab.slack.field.invite.help: Invite project members to the channel, matched by email to a Slack account. Best-effort — members without a matching Slack account are skipped.
collab.confirmDeleteGchat: Remove the Google Chat connector? The service account key and space settings will be cleared and provisioning disabled. Spaces already created are not affected.
collab.gchat.blurb: Creates a Google Chat space and invites the members, matched by email. Requires a Google Workspace service account with domain-wide delegation, impersonating a real Workspace user — Google Chat has no app-only mode for creating spaces and adding members.
collab.gchat.field.serviceAccountEmail.h: The …@…iam.gserviceaccount.com email of a Google Cloud service account with domain-wide delegation enabled for the chat.spaces and chat.memberships scopes.
collab.gchat.field.privateKey.label: Service account private key
collab.gchat.field.privateKey.help: The PKCS#8 PEM private key from the service account's JSON key file. Encrypted at rest, never shown again — leave empty to keep the current key.
collab.gchat.field.subjectEmail.label: Impersonated Workspace user
collab.gchat.field.subjectEmail.help: A real Google Workspace user the service account acts as (domain-wide delegation) — Google Chat requires a human actor to create spaces and add members, a service account alone cannot.
collab.gchat.field.spacePrefix.label: Space name prefix
collab.gchat.field.spacePrefix.help: Prepended to the project name, e.g. proj- → proj-Website revamp. Unlike Slack, Google Chat space names aren't slugified.
collab.gchat.field.invite.label: Invite members
collab.gchat.field.invite.help: Invite project members to the space, matched by email. Best-effort — members without a Chat account are skipped.
collab.gchat.field.authMode.label: Authentication
collab.gchat.field.authMode.help: How the app authenticates to Google. Workload Identity Federation needs no downloadable service account key — the recommended choice when your organization enforces the 'disable service account key creation' policy.
collab.gchat.field.wifAudience.label: Workload Identity pool audience
collab.gchat.field.wifAudience.help: Full resource name of the WIF provider: //iam.googleapis.com/projects/<num>/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/<pool>/providers/<provider>.
collab.gchat.wif.help: Keyless mode: generate a signing key below, paste its public JWKS into the WIF provider config in Google Cloud, then grant the pool principal roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the service account. No service account key is ever downloaded.
collab.gchat.wif.generated: Signing key generated. Paste the JWKS below into your WIF provider config.
collab.gchat.wif.issuer: Issuer (set as the provider's issuer URI)
collab.gchat.wif.jwks: Public JWKS (paste into the WIF provider)
collab.spBlurb: Let agents and invited members read a project team's SharePoint documents (live proxy, read-only). Reuses the Microsoft Teams Graph identity — only the identity model and, in selected_granter mode, a reader app are configured here.
collab.spNeedsTeams: Microsoft Teams provisioning is not configured yet — SharePoint reading relies on its Graph identity. Configure Microsoft Teams above (or a dedicated reader app in selected_granter mode) for reads to succeed.
collab.inboundHeading: Inbound — an external tool declares the space
collab.inbound.title: Declared spaces API
collab.inbound.blurb: For tools that create the space themselves (Slack, Google, or Teams managed outside Vaks): they declare the link back so it shows on the project. Uses an organization key restricted to linking only — it cannot modify anything else on the project.
collab.inbound.epPut: Declare or update a space (idempotent per project + provider). Refuses to overwrite a space provisioned by Vaks.
collab.inbound.epGet: List the spaces linked to a project.
collab.inbound.epDelete: Remove a declared link (external links only).
collab.inbound.triggerHint: Trigger: subscribe a webhook to the project.activated event to know when to create the space.
docsources.field.identityMode.label: Graph identity model
docsources.field.identityMode.help: read_all = one app with Sites.Read.All (a single consent, no per-site grant; vaks-pm restricts reads to provisioned teams). selected_granter = a minimal reader app (Sites.Selected) through which all agent reads flow; the provisioning app grants it read access on that team’s site only, automatically.
docsources.field.readerClientId.label: Reader app client ID (selected_granter)
docsources.field.readerClientId.help: GUID of the minimal reader app registration (Sites.Selected). Only used in the selected_granter model — leave empty for read_all.
docsources.field.readerClientSecret.help: Encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never shown again — leave empty to keep the current secret.
docsources.field.readerCertThumbprint.he: Secretless certificate auth for the reader app. Copy it from Entra > Certificates. Set it with the private key below — it then takes precedence over the reader secret.
docsources.field.readerPrivateKey.label: Reader private key (PEM PKCS#8)
docsources.field.readerPrivateKey.help: Private key matching the reader certificate. Encrypted at rest, never leaves the server. Leave empty to keep the current key.
section.agentTrustIssuers.title: Federated agent identity
section.agentTrustIssuers.blurb: Let agents authenticate with the token their own platform issues — no secret to distribute or rotate.
trustIssuers.blurb: Declare an issuer you trust. Agents present the JWT their platform gives them (Kubernetes, Entra workload identity, GitHub Actions); vaks-pm verifies it and exchanges it for a short-lived token. Public-key crypto — no secret is stored. A valid token never grants access on its own: the agent must already exist and have been activated by a human.
trustIssuers.deriveNote: Prefilled from the connector — review and confirm each field.
trustIssuers.derivedNote: Prefilled from connector « {{label}} ». Values are a one-time snapshot: changing the connector later will not update this issuer.
trustIssuers.deleteMsg: Delete « {{label}} »? Agents relying on it will no longer be able to authenticate.
trustIssuers.issuerHelp: Compared character-for-character with the token’s iss claim.
trustIssuers.audienceHelp: Required in the token’s aud claim. This is what stops a token the agent obtained for another app (e.g. Microsoft Graph) from being accepted here.
trustIssuers.idpSourceHelp: Provenance of the agents this issuer may authenticate. Must match the agent’s own idpSource — a defence-in-depth check.
trustIssuers.keysSection: Signing keys — one of the three
trustIssuers.discoveryHelp: Resolves the JWKS URI for you. Leave blank if you set the JWKS URI or paste the key set directly.
trustIssuers.jwksJsonHelp: Paste the key set to verify with no outbound call — recommended for an internal or air-gapped issuer. Key rotation becomes manual.
trustIssuers.subjectClaimHelp: Claim carrying the agent’s external id (default sub). Entra workload identity may need oid.
trustIssuers.defaultOwnerHelp: Human owner assigned to auto-declared agents. Required for auto-declare.
trustIssuers.constraintsHelp: Extra claims required, exact match. E.g. { "repository": "org/repo" } for GitHub Actions.
trustIssuers.autoDeclare: Auto-declare unknown agents (as draft, without a token)
agents.machineCredsHint: For a headless agent with no identity platform: a rotating refresh it exchanges for a short token on /agents/token, renewing itself. The secret is shown once — no browser, no user session.
agents.credShownOnce: Copy this now — it is shown only once.
collab.provisionHelp: Create the space for a project that is ALREADY active — the automatic trigger only fires when a project enters ACTIVE. Paste the project id. Idempotent: a project that already has a space is left untouched.
docsources.wif.help: Workload Identity Federation: no service-account key is stored. Generate the key below, then paste the public JWKS into your Google WIF provider config. Domain-wide impersonation is required.
docsources.wif.saveFirst: Save the connector first, then reopen it to generate the WIF key.
docsources.wif.generated: WIF key generated — paste the JWKS into your Google WIF provider.
docsources.wif.jwks: Public JWKS (paste into the WIF provider config)
collab.gdrive.blurb: Creates one Google shared drive per project — the Google equivalent of the SharePoint site that comes with a Teams team. Its documents then become readable from the project (read-only, through the Google Drive document source).
collab.confirmDeleteGdrive: Permanently delete this project's shared drive on Google? The files it contains will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
collab.gdrive.field.authMode.help: Service account key (downloaded JSON) or Workload Identity Federation (keyless). Provisioning needs the Drive write scope; reading documents stays read-only.
The service account that creates shared drives. It may differ from the one used to read documents.
collab.gdrive.field.subjectEmail.help: Impersonated Workspace user (domain-wide delegation). Required: a service account alone cannot create a shared drive. That user must be allowed to create shared drives.
collab.gdrive.field.drivePrefix.label: Drive name prefix
collab.gdrive.field.drivePrefix.help: Prepended to the project name, e.g. "Project " → "Project Website revamp".
collab.gdrive.field.memberRole.label: Role for added members
collab.gdrive.field.memberRole.help: Permission granted to project members on the shared drive. Viewer is enough for document context.
collab.gdrive.field.invite.label: Add project members
collab.gdrive.field.invite.help: Automatically adds project members (and members of assigned teams) to the shared drive, at creation and on every re-sync.
agentPolicies.briefDefaultDesc: House conventions inherited by every agent-enabled project, field by field: a project that fills a field wins, the others fall back here. Set your output language and format once instead of retyping them in each project.
